The central claim is wrong. Line 229 is `<Trash2 className="h-3.5 w-3.5" />` — the finding's own quotation ('aria-hidden-less icon') is a paraphrase, not the code. Under the HTML-AAM/accname algorithm, a button with no text content and no aria-label/aria-labelledby takes its accessible name from the title attribute, and this button carries one at :223-227 — so a screen-reader user does NOT hear an unnamed button, they hear either 'Inherited from the tenant — removing it affects every card' or 'Remove this binding', i.e. the warning reaches assistive tech, contradicting both sentences of the mechanism. (The lucide-react svg contributes no accessible text: it renders with no role and no title child.) What survives is narrow and cosmetic: title tooltips are not shown on keyboard focus in mainstream browsers and are unreachable on touch, so a sighted keyboard or touch operator sees no warning — a visible tone/label difference would be better. That is TRIVIAL, not MINOR. (Line 128, not 127, is the Priority aria-label.)
